LV.summary:
- **Brock Bowers (TE)** — ESPN’s read and the Raiders’ offseason framing both point to Klint Kubiak’s system and Kirk Cousins’ experience as reasons Bowers could post a career season after a down, injury-affected 2025. He still looks like the focal point of the passing game, which keeps him locked in as the top fantasy piece here. [7, 8]

- **Tre Tucker (WR)** — Tucker is being described as having a real chance to be the Raiders’ top wide receiver and the offense’s No. 2 passing-game option behind Bowers. That’s the clearest non-Bowers usage bump on the roster and gives him the strongest upside climb among the receivers. [1]

- **Michael Mayer (TE)** — Mayer is being cast as a “now or never” player who could settle in as a valuable second tight end in Klint Kubiak’s 12-personnel-heavy offense. That keeps him relevant as a secondary TE who could carve out structured volume, even with Bowers as the main target. [1]

- **Connor Heyward (FB)** — The Raiders are bringing back a true fullback, with Heyward announced at the spot and positioned as the player to beat. That matters for fantasy mainly because it signals a more traditional run-game structure that could shape how the backs are used. [2]

- **Aidan O'Connell (QB)** — O'Connell is projected to be the Raiders’ third/emergency quarterback behind Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza. That effectively wipes out any meaningful starting-path value unless the depth chart changes again. [1]

- **Cam Ward (QB)** — Tennessee is banking on offseason upgrades around Ward, and the offense was hindered last year by 25 dropped passes, fourth-most in the NFL. - **Jeffery Simmons (DT)** — Robert Saleh and the Titans plan to reduce Simmons’ snaps to keep him fresh for key one-on-one situations. That matters most in IDP formats, where a lighter snap load can trim weekly tackle volume even if his disruption stays high. [5]
